prose_changes.after: age, tumour size, number of positive lymph nodes, progesterone receptor measurement, oestrogen receptor measurement, hormonal therapy, menopausal status and tumour grade

prose_changes.before: The reconstruction procedure made a clear distinction between predictors and survival outcomes: GBSG2 time and cens, WHAS500 lenfol and fstat, and METABRIC time and event. Source fields were mapped to explicit binary event indicators according to their documented coding. In particular, the GBSG2 field named cens supplies the observed-event indicator. The cohort adapters standardised the representation to time and event, enabling a common survival-analysis interface across the three cohorts.
prose_changes.after: Survival outcomes were defined separately from the predictors. Each observation comprised a follow-up duration and a binary event indicator. Dataset-specific coding was checked before analysis so that one consistently denoted an observed event and zero denoted right censoring across all three cohorts.

prose_changes.before: \section{Reproducibility and Computational Integrity}
prose_changes.after: \section{Computational Implementation and Verification}

prose_changes.before: Reproducibility was supported by specified model configurations, fold definitions, preprocessing rules and deterministic seeds. The computational environment used Python 3.11.15, PyMC 5.28.5 \cite{pymc2023}, ArviZ 0.23.4 \cite{arviz2019}, scikit-survival 0.28.0 \cite{polsterl2020}, lifelines 0.30.3 \cite{lifelines2019}, PyTorch 2.13.0 \cite{pytorch2019} and pycox 0.3.0 \cite{pycox2019}. Reporting the software and diagnostic procedures alongside the mathematical model supports reproducible Bayesian analysis \cite{ref35,ref39,ref40,ref53}.
prose_changes.after: The analysis was implemented in Python. PyMC supported Bayesian model fitting \cite{pymc2023}, and ArviZ provided posterior diagnostics \cite{arviz2019}. CoxPH was fitted using lifelines \cite{lifelines2019}; scikit-survival supported the survival analyses and performance metrics \cite{polsterl2020}. DeepSurv used PyTorch \cite{pytorch2019} and pycox \cite{pycox2019}. Model settings, preprocessing and validation procedures were applied consistently across the comparisons \cite{ref35,ref39,ref40,ref53}.

prose_changes.before: Diagnostic summaries, fitted settings, preprocessing state, validation predictions and posterior summaries were retained for each outcome. Scientific reproduction checks compared all 450 original model--fold outcomes with repeated computations of their scientific outputs and diagnostic outcomes. Machine-dependent execution times were excluded from that comparison.
prose_changes.after: Numerical verification compared predictions, posterior summaries and diagnostic outcomes across all 450 original model--fold evaluations. Computation times were assessed separately from the agreement of the scientific estimates.
